a.t: Passage A: The Night Market App
a.x: When Farah's mother sold kuih at the night market, she often went home with unsold boxes. Farah, who was studying computer science, built a simple app that let regular customers pre-order before five o'clock. Within a month, waste dropped by almost half and her mother could plan exactly how much flour to buy. Other traders soon asked for the app, so Farah added a feature that showed each stall's location on a map. However, not everyone was pleased. Some older traders felt left behind because they did not own smartphones. Farah responded by running free weekend classes at the community hall. She says the project taught her that technology is only useful when it includes the people it is meant to serve.

b.x: The Malayan tapir, with its black front and white 'saddle', is one of the most unusual animals in our rainforests. Sadly, its numbers have fallen sharply. Forests are cleared for plantations and roads, and tapirs are often hit by vehicles when they cross highways at night. Conservationists have built wildlife viaducts so that animals can pass safely beneath busy roads. Camera traps show that tapirs use these crossings regularly. Experts argue that protecting forest corridors is more effective than creating isolated reserves, because tapirs need large areas to find food and mates. Public awareness also matters: drivers who slow down in signposted areas can save lives.

c.t: Passage C: A Letter of Complaint (extract)
c.x: Dear Sir, I am writing to express my concern about the condition of the bus stop outside SMK Taman Jaya. For the past three months, the roof has been leaking and the bench is broken. On rainy days, students are forced to stand in the open. Furthermore, the street light nearby does not work, which makes the area unsafe after co-curricular activities. I would be grateful if the council could repair the roof and the light as soon as possible. I look forward to your prompt reply. Yours faithfully, Nur Aina.

a.t: Passage A: The Night Market App
a.x: When Farah's mother sold kuih at the night market, she often went home with unsold boxes. Farah, who was studying computer science, built a simple app that let regular customers pre-order before five o'clock. Within a month, waste dropped by almost half and her mother could plan exactly how much flour to buy. Other traders soon asked for the app, so Farah added a feature that showed each stall's location on a map. However, not everyone was pleased. Some older traders felt left behind because they did not own smartphones. Farah responded by running free weekend classes at the community hall. She says the project taught her that technology is only useful when it includes the people it is meant to serve.

c.t: Passage C: A Letter of Complaint (extract)
c.x: Dear Sir, I am writing to express my concern about the condition of the bus stop outside SMK Taman Jaya. For the past three months, the roof has been leaking and the bench is broken. On rainy days, students are forced to stand in the open. Furthermore, the street light nearby does not work, which makes the area unsafe after co-curricular activities. I would be grateful if the council could repair the roof and the light as soon as possible. I look forward to your prompt reply. Yours faithfully, Nur Aina.
